children: traded lower on Wednesday after updated data from a mid-stage trial for ORKA-001, its candidate for the autoimmune skin condition plaque psoriasis, fell short of expectations.

Announcing 28-week data from its EVERLAST-A Phase 2a trial, the company said that ORKA-001, designed to treat plaque psoriasis with a less frequent dosing regimen, indicated a 71% PASI 100 response rate, a clinical tool used to measure the severity of psoriasis.
In April, the Menlo Park, California-based biotech said EVERLAST-A for patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis achieved the primary endpoint, with about 64% of trial subjects achieving PASI
The analysis conducted at six months after the last dose also indicated that the PASI 90 response rate, a key secondary endpoint of the trial, rose to 87% compared with 83% at Week 16.
said ORKA-001 continued to be well tolerated even though two patients had serious adverse events, which were considered unrelated to the experimental drug.
